connection_condition: League.country_id references Country.id
description: A country is composed of the leagues played in it. In this database the correspondence is one-to-one, so each country holds exactly one league.

connection_condition: Match.league_id references League.id
description: A league is composed of the matches played in it; a match cannot be interpreted without the league it belongs to.

connection_condition: Match.season labels the season of the match
description: A season is composed of the matches played within it; every match belongs to exactly one season.

connection_condition: Match.home_team_api_id and Match.away_team_api_id reference Team.team_api_id
description: A team's campaign is composed of the matches it played; every match is contributed by exactly two teams, one as home team and one as away team.

connection_condition: Match.home_team_goal holds the home score of that row
description: The home team goal count is a component of the match result; it has no meaning apart from its match.

connection_condition: Match.away_team_goal holds the away score of that row
description: The away team goal count is a component of the match result; it has no meaning apart from its match.
A draw is a specific kind of match outcome, so the set of drawn matches is a subset of all matches.

connection_condition: A match is a draw when its home team goal count equals its away team goal count
description: The draw outcome is derived by comparing the two goal counts of the match rather than being stored as a flag; counting draws means counting matches whose two goal counts are equal.

connection_condition: Player_Attributes.player_api_id references Player.player_api_id
description: A player is described by a series of dated attribute snapshots; a snapshot has no meaning without the player it rates.

connection_condition: Player.height holds the measurement on the player row
description: Height is a component measurement of the player record.

connection_condition: Player.weight holds the measurement on the player row
description: Weight is a component measurement of the player record.

connection_condition: Player.birthday holds the date of birth on the player row
description: The date of birth is a component attribute of the player record and is the basis for the player's age.

connection_condition: Age is the difference between the current date and the player's date of birth
description: The player's age is not stored; it is derived from the date of birth relative to the present date.

connection_condition: Both identifier spaces are carried on the player record and repeated on each attribute snapshot
description: The two identifier spaces name the same players under different naming conventions, so either can identify a player. They are not fully interchangeable as join keys: the API identifier covers every attribute snapshot while the FIFA API identifier leaves a small number of snapshots unmatched.
The database-local primary key and the external API identifier both denote the same player, but they are separate numbering systems with no shared values.

connection_condition: Player_Attributes.overall_rating belongs to the snapshot row
description: The overall rating is a component score of a player attribute snapshot.

connection_condition: Player_Attributes.potential belongs to the snapshot row
description: The potential score is a component score of a player attribute snapshot.

connection_condition: The ability columns belong to the snapshot row
description: The fine-grained ability scores are component measurements of a player attribute snapshot. This is the parent relation for the ability family; the individually named abilities the workload uses are also attached directly to the snapshot.

connection_condition: Player_Attributes.heading_accuracy belongs to the snapshot row
description: Heading accuracy is a component ability score of a player attribute snapshot.

connection_condition: Player_Attributes.jumping belongs to the snapshot row
description: Jumping is a component ability score of a player attribute snapshot.

connection_condition: Player_Attributes.long_shots belongs to the snapshot row
description: Long shots is a component ability score of a player attribute snapshot.

connection_condition: Player_Attributes.crossing belongs to the snapshot row
description: Crossing is a component ability score of a player attribute snapshot.

connection_condition: Player_Attributes.finishing belongs to the snapshot row
description: Finishing is a component ability score of a player attribute snapshot.

connection_condition: Player_Attributes.curve belongs to the snapshot row
description: Curve is a component ability score of a player attribute snapshot.

connection_condition: Player_Attributes.sprint_speed belongs to the snapshot row
description: Sprint speed is a component ability score of a player attribute snapshot.

connection_condition: Player_Attributes.preferred_foot belongs to the snapshot row
description: The preferred foot is recorded on the attribute snapshot rather than on the biographical player record, so foot preference is observed at snapshot dates.

connection_condition: Team_Attributes.team_api_id references Team.team_api_id
description: A team is described by a series of dated tactical snapshots; a snapshot has no meaning without its team.

connection_condition: Team_Attributes.buildUpPlaySpeed belongs to the snapshot row
description: The build-up play speed score is a component of a team tactical snapshot.

connection_condition: Team_Attributes.chanceCreationPassing belongs to the snapshot row
description: The chance creation passing score is a component of a team tactical snapshot.

connection_condition: Each class column is paired with the numeric score of the same snapshot row
description: The class label is the categorical reading of a numeric style score and is a component of the same team tactical snapshot.

Both are team tactical style scores measured on the same snapshot and sharing the same numeric scale and class-band boundaries, but they describe different aspects of play: tempo versus chance creation by passing. They frequently appear together because both are quoted to characterise a team's style.
Current strength and expected ceiling are quoted together on a player snapshot and share the same scale, but they answer different questions: observed level now versus projected maximum.
